guard: L5022: the walk refuses a recorded branch the edited source no longer declares
why: The complement of branch-digest.json, and it exists because that config's own narrowness
argument had a hole. The 'losers only' rule is justified by the walk ENTERING the winner: an
edit there diverges at the step it broke, which is a better error than 'some arm changed'. A
RENAME removes the arm, so there is no step left to diverge at and the justification quietly
What it did instead was worse than a silent pass. `race` filtered the source's arms down to the
recorded winner, got an empty list, and awaited `Promise.race([])` -- which never settles. A
migration or a fork over a renamed winning arm returned no verdict at all. `parallel` did not
hang, because `Promise.all([])` resolves, and handed the program back the recorded value keyed
by an arm the source no longer has.
TWO of the five mutations are in the PARANOID direction. A kill set whose every member makes the
guard quieter proves only that the suite notices a missing refusal; narrowness is the half that
keeps an edited race migratable at all, and the cells that defend it need their own mutations.
This suite counts rather than throws, so a mutation may redden more than the cell it names --
the harness requires the NAMED cell to be red, and the marker prints at the end because the
suite reaches it on every run.

mutations.name: the guard is skipped entirely: the walk enters nothing and awaits an empty race
mutations.find:
if (only !== undefined) {
        const present = new Set(all.map(([k]) => k));
mutations.replace:
if (false) {

mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: a walk into a recorded winning arm the edit renamed away RETURNS rather than hanging
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: a walk into a recorded winning arm the edit renamed away RETURNS rather than hanging
mutations.note: The cell carries its own deadline for exactly this mutation. Asserted with a bare `await`, removing the guard would HANG the suite rather than redden it, and the mutation would be graded on the harness's patience instead of on the guard.

mutations.name: the guard covers `race` only, where the hang made it obvious
mutations.expectRed: a parallel branch the edit renamed away is refused too, rather than completing silently
mutations.cell: a parallel branch the edit renamed away is refused too, rather than completing silently
mutations.note: The half that is easy to miss, because `parallel` never announced itself: `Promise.all([])` resolves, so the only symptom is a recorded value handed back under a key the source dropped. A guard written from the bug report alone would stop here.

mutations.name: PARANOID: the gap is computed the other way round -- source arms absent from `only`
mutations.expectRed: an unedited race still walks to completion
mutations.cell: an unedited race still walks to completion
mutations.note: Every decided race has a loser that is in the SOURCE and not in `only`, so this refuses every race ever recorded -- including one whose source did not change. The control cell is what catches it, which is why the control is not ceremony.

mutations.name: PARANOID: refuse when the arm COUNT changed rather than when a recorded name is absent
mutations.expectRed: and an arm the edit ADDED does not trip it: nothing recorded went missing
mutations.cell: and an arm the edit ADDED does not trip it: nothing recorded went missing
mutations.note: The second narrowness twin. Widening a race adds an arm and removes nothing recorded, so the walk must still complete; a count test cannot tell the two edits apart and makes every widened scope un-migratable.

mutations.name: the refusal fires with an empty payload, so it names no arm and no scope
mutations.expectRed: the refusal names the missing arm, the scope, and what the source does declare
mutations.cell: the refusal names the missing arm, the scope, and what the source does declare
mutations.note: The whole repair for this refusal is a NAME. An author told only 'this scope diverged' goes looking inside an arm's body, which is the one place nothing changed -- so the payload is the guard, not decoration on it.
